title: Real-Time E-Commerce Microservices DevOps Platform
description: End-to-end DevOps implementation for a real-time e-commerce microservices application, covering local development, containerization, AWS infrastructure provisioning, Kubernetes orchestration, networking, GitOps and automated CI/CD. The project demonstrates a production-oriented approach to deploying and managing a distributed application on AWS using Infrastructure as Code and declarative application delivery.
features: Real-time e-commerce application based on a microservices architecture
Local development environment using Docker Compose
Containerization of application microservices using Docker
AWS account and IAM configuration
EC2-based DevOps administration environment
AWS VPC and networking infrastructure
Infrastructure provisioning and management using Terraform
Terraform remote state management
Terraform backend configuration
Terraform state locking
Amazon EKS cluster provisioning using Terraform
Kubernetes deployment and service configuration
Kubernetes Ingress configuration
Ingress Controller setup for external application traffic
Kubernetes StorageClass configuration
PersistentVolume and PersistentVolumeClaim configuration
Application deployment and validation on Amazon EKS
Custom domain configuration using Amazon Route 53
DNS integration with the Kubernetes application endpoint
GitOps-based Kubernetes deployment using Argo CD
Continuous Integration using GitHub Actions
Automated Docker image build and publishing workflow
Integration of GitHub Actions with Argo CD
End-to-end CI/CD workflow from source code change to Kubernetes deployment
Documented deployment and operational workflow

architecture.overview: The platform follows a cloud-native architecture where application microservices are containerized with Docker and deployed to Amazon EKS. AWS infrastructure is provisioned through Terraform, while GitHub Actions provides continuous integration and Argo CD provides GitOps-based continuous delivery.
request_flow: End user accesses the e-commerce application through the custom domain
Amazon Route 53 resolves the application domain
External traffic reaches the AWS load balancer associated with the Kubernetes Ingress
Kubernetes Ingress routes requests to the appropriate microservice
Kubernetes Services provide stable networking to application workloads
Microservices run as Docker containers inside Amazon EKS
deployment_flow: Developer commits application changes to GitHub
GitHub Actions starts the CI workflow
Application dependencies are installed and build or validation steps are executed
Docker images are built for the affected microservice
Container images are tagged and pushed to Amazon ECR
Kubernetes deployment configuration is updated through the GitOps workflow
Argo CD detects the desired-state change in Git
Argo CD synchronizes the Kubernetes resources with Amazon EKS
The updated microservice is deployed to the Kubernetes cluster
infrastructure_flow: Terraform configuration defines AWS infrastructure as code
Terraform backend stores infrastructure state remotely
Terraform state locking prevents conflicting infrastructure changes
Terraform provisions networking and supporting AWS resources
Terraform provisions the Amazon EKS cluster and required configuration
Kubernetes resources are deployed after the cluster becomes available

aws_infrastructure.purpose: Configured AWS identities, roles and permissions required for infrastructure provisioning and platform operations.
Provides the network foundation for the Kubernetes environment and supporting AWS resources.
Controls inbound and outbound network traffic between infrastructure components.
Provides the managed Kubernetes control plane for running the e-commerce microservices.
Stores Docker container images used by the Kubernetes workloads.
Provides an administration and DevOps environment for working with AWS, Docker, Terraform and Kubernetes tooling.
Provides DNS management and maps the custom application domain to the application entry point.

terraform_implementation.description: Terraform is used as the Infrastructure as Code layer to provision and manage AWS infrastructure in a repeatable and version-controlled manner.
engineering_benefits: Ability to review infrastructure changes before applying them

containerization.description: The application microservices are packaged as Docker containers to provide consistent application execution across local development and Kubernetes environments.
workflow: Push application images to a container registry
containerization.local_development: Docker Compose is used to run the application and supporting services locally, providing a repeatable development and validation environment before Kubernetes deployment.

kubernetes_implementation.description: Amazon EKS is used as the container orchestration platform for running and managing the application microservices.
kubernetes_implementation.deployment_model: Each application microservice is deployed as a Kubernetes workload with a corresponding service providing internal connectivity. Ingress provides controlled external routing into the application platform.
validation: Review Kubernetes events and logs during troubleshooting

networking.description: The application networking layer connects the public DNS endpoint to the Kubernetes workloads through AWS and Kubernetes networking components.

storage.description: Kubernetes persistent storage resources are configured for workloads that require data persistence beyond the lifecycle of individual pods.
storage.objective: Provide Kubernetes workloads with persistent storage through declarative storage resources rather than tying application state to individual containers.

gitops.description: Argo CD is used to implement GitOps-based continuous delivery, with Git serving as the declarative source of truth for Kubernetes application configuration.
workflow: Kubernetes configuration is maintained in Git
Application image or deployment configuration is updated
Argo CD detects the desired-state change
Argo CD compares desired and actual cluster state
Amazon EKS runs the desired application version

ci_cd.description: GitHub Actions and Argo CD are combined to create an end-to-end CI/CD workflow from source code changes through container image creation and Kubernetes deployment.
continuous_integration: Application validation and build steps are executed
Container image is pushed to Amazon ECR
continuous_delivery: Deployment configuration references the new application image
GitOps repository represents the desired Kubernetes state
Amazon EKS deploys the updated workload
ci_cd.outcome: The resulting workflow reduces manual deployment activities and establishes a repeatable path from source-code change to Kubernetes deployment.

challenges: Designing a repeatable AWS infrastructure provisioning process
Managing Terraform state safely in a collaborative environment
Connecting application containerization with Kubernetes deployment
Configuring Kubernetes ingress and external traffic routing
Integrating AWS networking with Kubernetes networking
Managing persistent storage for Kubernetes workloads
Connecting custom DNS configuration with the Kubernetes application endpoint
Separating continuous integration from continuous delivery
Implementing GitOps without relying on manual Kubernetes deployments
Maintaining consistency between the desired Git state and the actual Kubernetes state
solutions: Used Terraform to define AWS infrastructure as code and reduce manual provisioning.
Configured remote Terraform state and state locking to improve infrastructure state management.
Used Docker to standardize application packaging across local and Kubernetes environments.
Used Amazon EKS as the managed Kubernetes platform for application workloads.
Implemented Kubernetes Deployments and Services for microservice orchestration and networking.
Configured Ingress and an Ingress Controller for centralized external HTTP routing.
Used Kubernetes storage resources for workloads requiring persistent data.
Integrated Route 53 with the application ingress endpoint for custom domain access.
Implemented GitHub Actions for automated continuous integration and container image publishing.
Implemented Argo CD to provide GitOps-based continuous delivery.
Used Git as the declarative source of truth for Kubernetes deployment configuration.

engineering_decisions.reason: Provides repeatable, version-controlled and reviewable AWS infrastructure provisioning.
Provides consistent application packaging across development and deployment environments.
Provides managed Kubernetes infrastructure for running the distributed microservices platform.
Provides an AWS-native registry for storing application container images.
Automates application validation, container builds and image publishing.
Provides declarative GitOps-based Kubernetes deployment and synchronization.
Provides managed DNS integration for the application custom domain.
Provides a consistent environment for running and validating the microservices application locally.

operational_workflow: Validate Terraform changes using terraform plan
Apply approved infrastructure changes using Terraform
Push container images to Amazon ECR
Allow Argo CD to synchronize the desired state
Validate application availability through the custom domain
Investigate logs, events and workload status when issues occur
troubleshooting_areas: Docker image build and registry issues
key_takeaways: Infrastructure can be managed as version-controlled code rather than manually through the AWS console.
Docker provides a consistent packaging model between local development and Kubernetes.
Amazon EKS provides a managed Kubernetes platform for distributed application workloads.
Kubernetes provides declarative deployment, service discovery and workload reconciliation.
Terraform enables repeatable infrastructure provisioning and environment reconstruction.
GitHub Actions automates continuous integration and container image delivery.
Argo CD provides a declarative GitOps model for Kubernetes continuous delivery.
The combination of CI and GitOps creates a repeatable application delivery pipeline.
Separating infrastructure management from application deployment improves maintainability and operational control.
The project demonstrates an end-to-end DevOps lifecycle rather than focusing on a single tool or platform.

portfolio_highlights: Designed an end-to-end DevOps workflow for a distributed microservices application.
Implemented AWS infrastructure using Infrastructure as Code.
Built a Kubernetes deployment platform on Amazon EKS.
Implemented GitOps-based application delivery with Argo CD.
Automated continuous integration with GitHub Actions.
Integrated container image delivery with Amazon ECR.
Configured Kubernetes ingress, persistent storage and external DNS.
Demonstrated production-oriented infrastructure, deployment and troubleshooting practices.
challenges_summary: The primary engineering challenge was creating a repeatable platform that connects infrastructure provisioning, containerization, Kubernetes orchestration and application delivery without relying on manual deployment processes. Particular attention was given to Terraform state management, AWS permissions, Kubernetes networking, ingress, persistent storage, DNS and the separation of CI from CD.
solution_summary: The solution combines Terraform for AWS Infrastructure as Code, Docker for application containerization, Amazon EKS for Kubernetes orchestration, Route 53 for DNS, GitHub Actions for continuous integration and Argo CD for GitOps-based continuous delivery. Together these components create an automated path from source-code changes to a validated application deployment on AWS.
